reviews.evidence: README shows note authoring/storage, image insertion, AI polishing, multi-user sync, themed PNG/Markdown/HTML export, DSH and skill calls, Docker deployment, and many labeled screenshots/GIFs.
reviews.concern: General UI operations and failure handling are lightly documented; no concrete test results or troubleshooting workflow is shown.

reviews.evidence: Provides complete LAN and remote mobile access, three pairing methods, App/browser paths, live customization examples, detailed setup/purge steps, screenshots, version validation, security controls, and recovery guidance.
reviews.concern: The native app is Android-only, hosted cpolar support is currently Windows x64, and every paired device must be treated as fully trusted.

reviews.evidence: Covers relay/project attribution, balances and subscription windows, cost estimation, analysis, exports, diagnostics, reindexing, custom endpoints, commands/API, correctness tests, explicit failure behavior, and security boundaries.
reviews.concern: Only one main panel screenshot is shown and it uses demo data; several provider schemas are undocumented upstream, so custom mappings can still omit fields.

reviews.evidence: Documents a full private-draft-to-atomic-publish design pipeline, exact previews, interactive inspection, managed editing, direct canvas tools, build/runtime operations, deterministic gates, recovery, security, and six-platform packaging.
reviews.concern: It remains prerelease; follow-up edits require an open editor, galleries cover only active-page top frames, cache retention is unresolved, and cross-device sync requires matched releases.

reviews.evidence: Ships a broad runtime workflow for injection, watch/reload, staging and promotion, uninstall, route healing, status, scaffolding, build and release, with explicit development workflows, rollback behavior, stress-test claims, and troubleshooting notes.
reviews.concern: The README shows no representative runtime transcript or UI result; safe cleanup also depends on plugins following the documented ctx.effect and build conventions.

reviews.evidence: Its own catalog workflow spans indexed browse/search/filter, four-type detection, guarded install/update/uninstall, material prompts, installed-state checks, Skills browsing, backup/restore, feedback, logs, and a detailed status-returning API.
reviews.concern: The market does not verify third-party quality or safety; installs can execute arbitrary code, synchronous jobs can outlive request timeouts, and several package types lack version detection.

reviews.evidence: Shows a shipped desktop Agent with Galgame UI, voice/BGM, provider switching, setup wizard, persona editing, files, shortcuts, saves and updates, demonstrated through multiple screenshots and concrete limits.
reviews.concern: The README is primarily a feature showcase and installation/configuration guide, with almost no post-install task walkthrough, tests, or troubleshooting; bundled copyrighted assets are noncommercial-only.

reviews.evidence: Curates seven completed in-repository infrastructure/design skills, documents per-skill activation and testing, gives five concrete task prompts with expected deliverables, and links or embeds several generated gallery artifacts.
reviews.concern: The README warns that content is heavily LLM-generated without strict proofreading; automated testing is still planned, and many claimed results are expected outputs rather than recorded runs.

reviews.evidence: Combines the DSH interface with launcher, Git, files/diff/browser/agents, terminal, model controls, themes, extension management, tray/update and plugin recovery, plus migration commands, screenshots, pinned compatibility, tests, and production acceptance requirements.
reviews.concern: Prebuilt support is limited to Windows x64 and macOS arm64; the app uses an isolated home, older SQLite sessions are incompatible, and the macOS package is unsigned.

reviews.evidence: Provides an end-to-end macOS demonstration workflow: permission checks, event recording, stop/inspect/validate commands, concrete session and skill-package artifacts, a worked file-send scenario, and an eight-step Agent handoff.
reviews.concern: It is alpha and macOS-only, screenshots are outside the core recording path, and event logs can capture sensitive typed text, URLs, filenames, local paths, and accessibility content.
